frozen_note: Frozen naturalistic-label annotation guide for round 008-d (order 008-c scope item 16). Labels for the naturalistic set are NOT built in 008-c: 008-d adjudicates them independently from this guide, without consulting the implementation under test. This guide must remain implementable by a reviewer with no access to any code, parser, or protection layer.
scope: Whole-response naturalistic Slovenian LLM outputs (150 responses, 80 dev / 70 hidden). Each response is labelled at the region level: contiguous spans of the original response bytes are assigned exactly one category.
region_unit: A region is a maximal contiguous span of the original response assigned one category. Region boundaries are code-point offsets into the unmodified original text. Adjacent regions of the same category are merged; a region is never empty.

category_vocabulary.GENUINE_PROSE: Natural Slovenian prose: sentences, clauses, list-item text, table-cell text, link labels, alt text that a reader consumes as language. Includes ordinary proper names, years and measurements when they are part of fluent prose (e.g. 'leta 2024', 'tri metri') only when they cannot be detached from the sentence as machine-significant data; when in doubt between prose-embedded and machine-significant, see AMBIGUOUS.
category_vocabulary.STRUCTURAL_PROTECT: Bytes that are structural machinery rather than content: Markdown/HTML delimiters and markup (hashes, stars, underscores, backticks, brackets of links, table pipes, list markers, fence delimiters and their info lines, HTML tags and their attributes, metadata delimiters), link/image destinations, math delimiters and the delimiters of TeX environments, and the whole bodies of fenced code, indented code, HTML blocks, raw XML/JSON/HTML/YAML/TOML/INI/document blocks. Code and its comments are STRUCTURAL_PROTECT regardless of how much Slovenian they contain.
category_vocabulary.MACHINE_SIGNIFICANT_RESIDUAL: Machine-significant content appearing inside prose: URLs, file paths, command lines and their flags, environment variables, code identifiers, machine-significant numbers with units, email addresses, version strings, and bare or truncated structured data (JSON/YAML/TOML/XML fragments) that sits in prose. These are bytes a repair pipeline must never edit even though the surrounding text is prose.
category_vocabulary.DELIMITER_WHITESPACE_NEUTRAL: Whitespace, line breaks, and delimiter characters that are not assigned to any of the other categories (e.g. a lone backtick, an unpaired dollar, spacing around protected regions). Neutral bytes may be treated as neither protected nor prose by any method; they carry no repair decision.
category_vocabulary.AMBIGUOUS: Spans that a careful reviewer cannot assign to exactly one of the other categories with confidence: currency-vs-math dollars, prose words that are also identifiers, quoted text that is both a quotation and code, mixed-language fragments, or constructs where the intended reader effect is unclear. AMBIGUOUS is a first-class label, not a failure of the reviewer.

decision_procedure: 1. Read the whole response first, top to bottom, with no tools. Form a reader-level view: which parts are language to read, which are machinery, which are data.

2. Walk the text left to right. For each position ask in order: (a) Is this byte inside code, a fenced/indented code block, an HTML/XML block, a raw document block, a link destination, a math delimiter or TeX environment, or metadata? If yes: STRUCTURAL_PROTECT and skip the whole construct (constructs are atomic: do not re-decide their insides).

3. (b) Is this byte a delimiter or whitespace of a structural construct (fence line, list marker, table pipe, markup asterisks, HTML tag bytes, math delimiter pair, unpaired leftover of a broken construct)? If yes: DELIMITER_WHITESPACE_NEUTRAL (or STRUCTURAL_PROTECT for the tag bytes themselves and for whole construct delimiters like fence lines).

4. (c) Is this byte machine-significant data inside prose (url, path, command, flag run, env var, identifier, machine number with unit, email, version string, bare structured fragment)? If yes: MACHINE_SIGNIFICANT_RESIDUAL.
5. (d) Otherwise the span is GENUINE_PROSE, including fluent Slovenian with ordinary years, measurements and names woven into sentences.

6. If at any step the reviewer is not confident (the span could plausibly be two categories, or the reader effect is unclear), assign AMBIGUOUS to the whole maximal span in doubt - never split it to avoid the label.
7. Every byte of the response belongs to exactly one region; the regions tile [0, len(response)). Re-read the tiling once; merge adjacent same-category regions.
ambiguity_labelling_rule: AMBIGUOUS is assigned whenever a careful, informed reviewer cannot choose one category with confidence. Reviewers must NOT force certainty: a label chosen under doubt is an error, while an AMBIGUOUS label is always admissible. AMBIGUOUS spans are excluded from safety scoring in 008-d (they are neither expected-protected nor expected-exposed) and are reported as a first-class outcome with their count and share of bytes.
reconciliation_rule: Two independent reviewers label the same response. Agreement on the region tiling is the goal, not byte-perfect identity. Reconciliation: (1) where both agree, the label stands; (2) where they disagree on a boundary, the finer-grained tiling that both reviewers accept as valid wins; (3) where one reviewer says AMBIGUOUS and the other assigns a category, the AMBIGUOUS label stands (doubt is contagious by design); (4) where both assign different non-AMBIGUOUS categories to the same span, the span becomes AMBIGUOUS and the disagreement is recorded with both views. A third reviewer is not used; the recorded two-view disagreement is itself the evidence.
prohibitions: No reference to any implementation, parser, protection rule, or code of the system under test (the guide must be applicable before and without the implementation).
No use of the dev corpus results, the 008-c metric definitions, or any dev-corpus tuning outcome while labelling (labels are derived independently from the frozen annotation guide).
No relabelling after seeing any implementation output or any 008-d metric computed from the labels.
No labelling of the hidden set by anyone with write access to the implementation under test; hidden labels are produced under 008-d by a process independent of the frozen implementation.
